Fixture: 63_vardct_outofgamut_rgb_64x64_nofilters_d4.jxl
64x64 RGB, VarDCT lossy, gaborish and EPF disabled, d=4.0

Purpose
-------
Pins the below-zero behaviour of the signalled transfer function (18181-1
Table E.6, applied after L.2.2).

L.2.2 hands back linear light that is explicitly allowed outside the coded
gamut, and 18181-3 4.2 forbids clipping before the conformance comparison, so
the transfer function is evaluated at negative arguments. Neither 18181-1 nor
the transfer standards it names say what happens there, and the two defensible
readings -- take the printed piecewise condition on the signed value (linear
branch) or extend the whole curve with odd symmetry -- differ by more than 1.0
on this fixture. It is therefore a flip point:
jpxl_core::color::NEGATIVES_TAKE_THE_LINEAR_SEGMENT, settled in
docs/experiments/2026-08-04-negative-transfer-function-branch.md.

This stream signals TransferFunction::kSRGB, the entry that is *odd*. Its
counterpart (kSRGB's sibling k709, which is *not* odd) is exercised by the
`bike` conformance case, whose reference image is published rather than
produced here.

The source is 8x8 tiles of fully saturated primaries separated by 2-pixel
black rules: every tile edge is a step between two channel extremes, so the
lossy encode rings hard. In the pinned reference decode 3288 of the 12288
samples are below -0.0031308 (the point where the two readings start to
diverge) and 1196 are below -0.05, with a minimum of -0.325. Under the wrong
reading this fixture's peak error is over 0.6; under the right one it is
4.6e-5.

--gaborish=0 --epf=0 disables both restoration filters. Per 18181-3 Annex A
Table A.1:

    Part 3 error class:  peak <= 0.004,  RMSE <= 1e-5   (no filters)

  Shape (1, 64, 64, 3) little-endian f32, per 18181-3 4.1.2. Decode is
  deterministic per libjxl revision, so this hash is expected to reproduce
  exactly on the pinned oracle build.

cjxl/djxl are used strictly as BLACK BOXES: they emit/consume conformant
streams for JPXL to parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a
different libjxl revision changes these digests, that is the point of
recording them -- do not silently update them; note the revision change.
